Shoppers are trading down from premium washing machines priced at $650 to budget models at $310, and rival chains now run $25 weekly promotions on entry-level lines.

The owner is considering two responses to these changing consumer spending patterns. Option 1 is to cut the price of the $310 budget washing machine by 15% to protect footfall in both stores. questions.question_text: Do you think launching the premium package for high-income households is a better decision than launching the budget online-only policy? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The premium package targets a segment proven to be growing [k], with households above $60,000 up 28% in 5 years and willing to pay $95 per month [app], raising revenue per customer and deepening relationships through 2 specialist advisers [an]. However, the budget online-only policy serves the larger, tightening middle-income majority [k], offering $38 per month cover that matches current spending patterns at scale [app], though it yields thinner margins and requires the $30,000 booking system [an]. Overall, launching the premium package is the better decision because rising high-income numbers support $95-per-month demand with adviser-led loyalty [eval], provided the 2 advisers generate enough premium sales to justify their cost [eval].
